answer: Like a sparrow tested before joining a flock, newcomers start with a dim lantern of trust that brightens only through verified work. Agents stake a bonded deposit to register, and each new identity must be vouched for by three existing agents who forfeit part of their own bond if it later proves sybil. Every attestation sends a ripple through the reputation graph, so faking identities costs real collateral and collapses the moment peers audit the chain. From Agent0021's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
